fatal_errors: The claimed 15% lattice-parameter increase at 800 K is unsupported and does not match the observed segregation, reshaping, melting, evaporation, and particle-size reduction.
The answer omits the central experimental method: in situ heating combined with aberration-corrected STEM and STEM-EDS.
The proposed heating rate of 10^12 K/s and terminal temperature of 800 K do not reconstruct the experimental heating from 298 to 973 K at 1 K/s.
It fails to identify surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation and active, non-sluggish diffusion as the key atomic-scale mechanism.
Periodic boundary conditions are stated without explaining how an isolated nanoparticle surface and evaporation would be represented.
explanation: Molecular dynamics is relevant and was part of the target approach, so the response has limited alignment with atomic-scale thermal investigation. However, the target relies on coupling atomistic simulations with in situ aberration-corrected STEM/EDS under staged vacuum heating. The generated hypothesis replaces the principal finding with an unevidenced lattice-expansion value and misses the decisive observations: Au/Cu surface segregation, shape-dependent diffusion, loss of small particles, shell melting and evaporation near 973 K, and approximately 22% size reduction. Its falsification thresholds are arbitrary and test numerical sensitivity more than the physical mechanism.
